theme: Weather, hurricanes, wildfires, disasters: NOAA/NHC tracks, EM-DAT, FEMA declarations, wildfire perimeters (Maui, LA fires), heatwaves; tourism-shock datasets

candidates.name: disasters (Measuring Economic Disruption from Climate Disasters)
candidates.what_it_holds: Replication package for paper measuring selection into the EM-DAT disaster record against MODIS burned-area and IBTrACS (hurricane) wind-field data. Repo holds bundled data as split archives (Climate_damage_full.bundle.part00/01, Climate_damage_repo.tar.gz.part00/01) plus code; README describes a 1,174-row register linking every number in the paper to its source (EM-DAT entry, MODIS burned area, IBTrACS wind fields, separating entry/monetisation/magnitude margins). No stars yet, updated 24 Aug 2026.
candidates.why_useful: Directly usable for gap 11 (hurricanes/wildfires as tourism shocks) and gap 17 (methods/event-study/replication packages): gives a rigorous, sourced EM-DAT-vs-satellite cross-walk that could be adapted to flag disaster severity for ABNB-relevant markets (Maui, LA, Gulf Coast, Caribbean) rather than relying on raw EM-DAT counts alone.
candidates.size_hint: multi-part bundle + tar.gz archives (exact size unknown, split into parts suggesting >100MB)
candidates.time_coverage: not fully specified; EM-DAT/IBTrACS/MODIS overlap era (~2000s-2020s)

candidates.name: fema-mcp-server
candidates.what_it_holds: MCP (Model Context Protocol) server / API client exposing FEMA OpenFEMA endpoints: disaster declarations, public-assistance grants, individual/household housing aid, and NFIP flood-insurance claims. Actively maintained TypeScript project (docs/, tests/, CI, package.json), last updated 24 Aug 2026, Apache-2.0.
candidates.why_useful: Turns FEMA's official disaster-declaration and NFIP flood-claims feeds into a clean, scriptable pull for gap 11 (hurricanes/wildfires/floods as shocks to specific STR markets) and could be repointed to pull county-level declarations timed against Airbnb market calendars.
candidates.size_hint: small (source code only, no committed data)
candidates.time_coverage: current OpenFEMA API coverage (1953-present per OpenFEMA)

candidates.name: fema-disaster-declarations-summaries
candidates.what_it_holds: Rearc's standard 'data-as-code' pattern repo for the OpenFEMA Disaster Declarations Summaries v2 dataset: init.sh + pre-processing/ scripts that pull the dataset (also republished on AWS Data Exchange), plus dataset-description.md and product-description.md documenting fields. No raw CSV committed directly in the repo root (confirmed via directory listing: only scripts/docs, no data files).
candidates.why_useful: A ready-made, documented pipeline to the full historical FEMA disaster-declarations table (all US disaster types back to the 1950s) for gap 11; complements the FEMA-MCP client above with a batch/ETL-oriented approach.
candidates.size_hint: scripts only; source dataset is tens of thousands of rows

candidates.name: catastrophe-risk-dashboard
candidates.what_it_holds: Streamlit catastrophe-risk dashboard with an actually-committed data file `emdat_disasters.xlsx` (confirmed via directory listing) plus `Cat modelling.py` and `Disaster dashboard.py`. Small hobby project, 0 stars, updated 12 Mar 2026.
candidates.why_useful: A directly downloadable EM-DAT extract (global disaster records incl. storms/floods/wildfires) already committed to a repo rather than requiring an EM-DAT account signup, useful as a quick cross-check source for gap 11 regional shock timing (LatAm/APAC per gaps 7/11).
candidates.size_hint: one xlsx file, likely a few thousand rows (typical EM-DAT extract)
candidates.time_coverage: unspecified EM-DAT vintage (likely 2000s-2020s based on typical extracts)

candidates.name: Earth-Engine-Wildfire-Data
candidates.what_it_holds: Python toolkit for downloading, processing, and preparing wildfire perimeter data from Google Earth Engine (GEE), supporting both historical and forecasted wildfire datasets; generates config files for wildfire modeling workflows. MIT licensed, 4 stars, updated 22 Nov 2025.
candidates.why_useful: A scriptable, non-Airbnb-site method to pull historical wildfire perimeters (could target Maui 2023 and LA Jan 2025 fires specifically) for gap 11 tourism-shock timing/severity, more current than static NIFC/GeoMAC dumps.
candidates.size_hint: code only, pulls data on demand from GEE
candidates.geography: global (wherever GEE fire products cover, incl. US)

candidates.name: datacenters-wildfires
candidates.what_it_holds: Interactive map site combining US data-center locations with historical wildfire perimeters (NIFC/WFIGS, 2016-Sep 2026) per its description. Directory listing shows only `us_data_centers_100mw_plus.csv` and an HTML map committed; wildfire perimeter data itself is pulled live from the NIFC/WFIGS API, not stored in-repo. Updated 10 Sep 2026 (very fresh).
candidates.why_useful: Confirms NIFC/WFIGS as a live, current (through Sep 2026) wildfire-perimeter API worth querying directly for gap 11 (Maui/LA fires and any 2026 wildfire events); the repo itself is not a data store but demonstrates a working integration pattern.
candidates.size_hint: one small CSV + one HTML file; no wildfire data committed

candidates.name: noaastormevents (CRAN mirror)
candidates.what_it_holds: Read-only GitHub mirror of the CRAN R package `noaastormevents`, an R client for exploring NOAA's Storm Events Database (1950-present: tornadoes, hurricanes/tropical storms, floods, hail, high wind, wildfire, heat, etc., county-level with property/crop damage estimates).
candidates.why_useful: Gives a clean, maintained R interface to the authoritative NOAA county-level storm-events feed (hurricanes, wildfires, heatwaves all included as event types) for gap 11; could be used to build a county-to-STR-market crosswalk for shock timing/severity.
candidates.license: not specified in listing (CRAN package, check upstream)
candidates.size_hint: package code only; source DB has 1.7M+ records per a related repo's description

candidates.name: census-fema-tornadoes
candidates.what_it_holds: MIT-licensed how-to repo for pulling and integrating tornado-track data with FEMA disaster declarations and Census geography. Small project (0 stars), updated 9 Sep 2025.
candidates.why_useful: A worked example of joining disaster declarations to census geography, a pattern reusable for mapping any FEMA-declared hurricane/wildfire county to nearby Inside Airbnb / STR markets for gap 11.

candidates.name: post-disaster-mobility-public
candidates.what_it_holds: Public-data pipeline linking FEMA National Risk Index (NRI), CDC Social Vulnerability Index (SVI), Census PUMA geographies, and FEMA disaster declarations through to IPUMS migration-PUMA level, i.e. models post-disaster population mobility/migration. Updated 15 Apr 2026, 'other' license.
candidates.why_useful: Post-disaster migration/mobility flows are a proxy for demand disruption and displacement travel (short-term-rental usage spikes for displaced residents) around hurricanes/wildfires, relevant to gap 11 and gap 20 (mobility/geospatial proxies).
candidates.size_hint: pipeline/code scale, sources IPUMS + FEMA NRI + CDC SVI + Census

candidates.name: thesis-flood-impact-analysis-2025
candidates.what_it_holds: MS thesis (Colorado State University) processing pipeline and analysis code measuring flood-disaster impacts using MODIS satellite imagery, climate data, and EM-DAT disaster records. MIT licensed, 5 stars, updated 10 Sep 2026 (very fresh/active).
candidates.why_useful: An actively maintained academic replication-style pipeline joining MODIS satellite flood extent with EM-DAT records; the method (not necessarily a large committed dataset) could be repurposed for hurricane-driven flooding impacting specific tourism markets (gap 11).
candidates.size_hint: code/pipeline; unclear if raw MODIS/EM-DAT data is committed
candidates.geography: global (wherever EM-DAT flood records + MODIS overlap)

candidates.name: Natural-Disasters-CSV-Agent
candidates.what_it_holds: Natural-language chatbot (FastMCP server + LangChain ReAct agent) built over what its description calls 'the EM-DAT disasters dataset (1900-2021)' as a CSV, answering questions with Plotly charts/HTML/tables. Updated 21 Jun 2026, not yet verified via directory listing whether the full CSV is committed vs. fetched.
candidates.why_useful: If the underlying CSV is committed, it is a long-run (1900-2021) global EM-DAT extract, i.e. older/longer than a typical fresh EM-DAT pull, useful background for gap 11 tourism-shock base rates by country/decade.
candidates.size_hint: unverified, described as full EM-DAT 1900-2021 CSV

candidates.name: fema-disaster-information
candidates.what_it_holds: FEMA Disaster Declarations and Public Assistance data-analysis repo, MIT licensed, 5 stars, updated 9 Jul 2025 (most-starred general-purpose FEMA-declarations analysis repo found in this sweep).
candidates.why_useful: Reasonably popular, MIT-licensed reference implementation for pulling/analysing OpenFEMA declarations and public-assistance grant data, another route into gap 11 with more community traction than the rearc-data pipeline repo.

queries_run: gh search repos "hurricane tracks dataset" --sort stars
gh search repos "fema disaster declarations" --sort stars
gh search repos "NOAA storm events database" --sort stars
notes: GitHub is thin on committed, large, ready-to-use disaster/weather datasets for this theme: most repos are analysis/dashboard/tutorial code that pulls FEMA OpenFEMA, EM-DAT, or NOAA data at runtime rather than storing it. The strongest find is andreiosiptsov/disasters, an active academic replication package (Aug 2026) cross-walking EM-DAT entries against MODIS burned-area and IBTrACS wind-field data with a sourced 1,174-row register -- this is a genuinely new methodological asset, not a duplicate of anything in CONTEXT.md. No dedicated NOAA/NHC HURDAT2 or NIFC/WFIGS *data-mirror* repo with large committed files turned up in six gh search calls (HURDAT2-analysis and datacenters-wildfires both turned out to be code-only, pulling from the live source instead of storing it) -- if another scout has WebSearch budget, it is worth checking Zenodo/Kaggle mirrors of HURDAT2 and NIFC historical perimeters directly rather than GitHub. EM-DAT itself gated behind a login on its own site, so committed xlsx/csv extracts on GitHub (Msimotwq, and the unverified bntdeep 1900-2021 CSV) are the only 'no-signup' EM-DAT routes found. Heatwave-specific and Maui/LA-fire-specific dedicated repos did not surface distinctly in the general wildfire/FEMA queries; a targeted follow-up search on 'Maui wildfire data' or 'Los Angeles fires 2025 dataset' specifically, plus a Zenodo/DOI search for HURDAT2 mirrors, would be the next places to look. Did not hit any rate limits during this run.
